key_insight: RECONTEXT improves long-context reasoning by recursively replaying query-relevant evidence from the original context before final answer generation, without training or pruning.
engineering_relevance: It offers a lightweight inference-time harness for systems that need better use of long documents while preserving the full context window.
method: Uses model-internal relevance signals to build a query-conditioned evidence pool.
Recursively replays selected evidence ahead of generation while keeping the full original context available.
Separates evidence organization from answer generation with no extra training or external memory.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on eight long-context datasets at 128K context length and consistently improved evidence utilization across Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Llama3-8B, with the best average rank on all three backbones.
watch_item: Because it relies on internal relevance signals and extra replay steps, performance may depend on the quality of the base model’s attention signals and can add inference overhead.
paper_title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
